source_records.title: H-GEN Spray: A Theoretical Genetic Therapy and Lipid Nanoparticle-Based Nasal Delivery System for Hantavirus Elimination
source_records.abstract: वैज्ञानिक शोध प्रस्ताव: हंतावायरस के विरुद्ध रिवर्स जेनेटिक्स और लिपिड-आधारित नेज़ल स्प्रे तकनीकअवधारणा एवं लेखक: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)विषय: वायरोलॉजी एवं बायो-मेडिकल इंजीनियरिंग (Theoretical Concept)1. परिचय (Introduction)हंतावायरस (Hantavirus) एक गंभीर वैश्विक स्वास्थ्य संकट है, जो मुख्य रूप से मनुष्यों के श्वसन तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है। वर्तमान में इसके सटीक इलाज के लिए शोध जारी हैं। इस लेख में, लेखक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा हंतावायरस को निष्क्रिय करने और उसे शरीर के भीतर ही नष्ट करने के लिए एक त्रि-स्तरीय जेनेटिक और नैनो-पार्टिकल आधारित चिकित्सा प्रणाली का प्रस्ताव रखा गया है।2. मुख्य सिद्धांत: L, M, और S खंडों का विलोपन (Targeting L, M, S Segments)हंतावायरस का जीनोम तीन प्रमुख आरएनए (RNA) खंडों से बना होता है: L (Large) जो रेप्लिकेशन एंजाइम बनाता है, M (Medium) जो बाहरी ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन कवच तैयार करता है, और S (Small) जो न्यूक्लियोकैप्सिड प्रोटीन बनाता है।इस परिकल्पना के अनुसार, वायरस के इन तीनों प्राकृतिक खंडों के जेनेटिक कोड को उलट (Invert) या बदल दिया जाएगा। इससे वायरस अपनी प्रतिकृति (Photocopy) बनाने की क्षमता खो देगा और बीमारी फैलाने के लायक नहीं रहेगा। 3. आणविक कार्यप्रणाली और एंजाइम प्रक्रिया (Molecular Mechanism Flowchart)इस जेनेटिक बदलाव को अंजाम देने के लिए आधुनिक मॉलिक्यूलर बायोलॉजी के उपकरणों और एंजाइमों का उपयोग निम्नलिखित फ्लोचार्ट के अनुसार प्रस्तावित है:[Virus RNA] ➔ (Reverse Transcriptase) ➔ [cDNA] ➔ (CRISPR/Restriction Enzymes) ➔ [Invert/Change Code] ➔ (RNA Polymerase) ➔ [Modified Inactive Virus] स्टेप 1 (Reverse Transcriptase): सबसे पहले हंतावायरस के प्राकृतिक RNA को 'रिवर्स ट्रांसक्रिप्टेज' एंजाइम की मदद से cDNA (Complementary DNA) में बदला जाएगा, ताकि लैब में इस पर काम करना आसान हो सके।स्टेप 2 (CRISPR/Restriction Enzymes): इसके बाद मॉलिक्यूलर कैंची (CRISPR-Cas या Restriction Enzymes) का उपयोग करके L, M, और S खंडों के विशिष्ट हिस्सों को काटा जाएगा।स्टेप 3 (Invert/Change Code): कटे हुए जेनेटिक कोड के अनुक्रम (Sequence) को उलट दिया जाएगा ताकि वायरस का मूल सिस्टम ब्लॉक हो जाए।स्टेप 4 (RNA Polymerase): अंत में, 'आरएनए पॉलीमरेज' एंजाइम द्वारा इस बदले हुए DNA से पुनः एक निष्क्रिय, हानिरहित वायरस (Modified Inactive Virus) तैयार किया जाएगा। 4. डिलीवरी माध्यम: लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल नेज़ल स्प्रे (Delivery System)इस संशोधित निष्क्रिय कोड को मानव शरीर में सुरक्षित रूप से पहुँचाने के लिए लेखक ने नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) का माध्यम चुना है।ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन कवच और लिपिड: इस कोड को वसा (Lipid) के एक सुरक्षात्मक कवच (Lipid Nanoparticle) में लपेटा जाएगा।यह स्प्रे नाक के रास्ते सीधे फेफड़ों और श्वसन नली (Respiratory Tract) तक पहुँचेगा, जो हंतावायरस का मुख्य हमला क्षेत्र है। शरीर में जाकर यह एक एंटीबॉडी की तरह काम करेगा और असली वायरस को आगे बढ़ने से रोक देगा। वैज्ञानिक शोध लेख: हंतावायरस रोधी जेनेटिक थेरेपी और लिपिड नेज़ल स्प्रे (H-GEN Spray)मुख्य आविष्कारक (Lead Innovator): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)क्षेत्र: वायरोलॉजी, मॉलिक्यूलर बायोलॉजी एवं नैनो-मेडिसिन (सैद्धांतिक मॉडल)1. प्रस्तावना (Introduction)हंतावायरस (Hantavirus) मुख्य रूप से फेफड़ों और श्वसन प्रणाली पर हमला करता है, जिससे हंतावायरस पल्मोनरी सिंड्रोम (HPS) जैसी जानलेवा बीमारियां होती हैं। वर्तमान में इसका कोई सटीक इलाज उपलब्ध नहीं है। आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा तैयार यह शोध लेख एक ऐसी अत्याधुनिक चिकित्सा पद्धति का प्रस्ताव करता है, जो वायरस के जेनेटिक कोड (L, M, S खंडों) को निष्क्रिय कर, एक लिपिड-आधारित नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) के माध्यम से सीधे फेफड़ों तक दवा पहुँचाती है। 2. इस आविष्कार के मुख्य फायदे और लाभ (Key Advantages & Benefits)बंटी कुमावत के इस फॉर्मूले के पारंपरिक दवाओं और टीकों की तुलना में निम्नलिखित बड़े फायदे हैं:सटीक निशाना (Targeted Delivery): हंतावायरस सीधे सांस की नली और फेफड़ों को प्रभावित करता है। यह फॉर्मूला नेज़ल स्प्रे के माध्यम से सीधे संक्रमित क्षेत्र (Target Organ) पर पहुँचता है, जिससे दवा पूरे शरीर में फैलने के बजाय सीधे फेफड़ों में काम शुरू कर देती है।वायरस की फोटोकॉपी (Replication) पर पूर्ण रोक: वायरस के L खंड को ब्लॉक करने के कारण वायरस शरीर की कोशिकाओं के अंदर अपनी संख्या (Replication) नहीं बढ़ा पाता। संख्या न बढ़ने से बीमारी तुरंत रुक जाती है।भविष्य के म्यूटेशन से सुरक्षा: यह थेरेपी वायरस के किसी एक हिस्से पर नहीं, बल्कि उसके तीनों बुनियादी खंडों (L, M, S) पर एक साथ हमला करती है। यदि वायरस अपना रूप बदलता (Mutate होता) भी है, तो भी वह इस थेरेपी से बच नहीं सकता।शारीरिक सुरक्षा और कम साइड इफेक्ट्स: इसमें उपयोग किया जाने वाला बाहरी आवरण प्राकृतिक लिपिड (वसा) का है, जिसे मानव शरीर आसानी से स्वीकार कर लेता है। इससे पारंपरिक दवाओं की तरह शरीर के अन्य अंगों (जैसे लिवर या किडनी) पर कोई दुष्प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।तीव्र प्रतिरक्षा (Fast-Acting Immunity): यह स्प्रे शरीर में जाते ही एंटीबॉडीज की तरह सक्रिय रूप से असली वायरस को ढूंढकर उसे काटना शुरू कर देता है, जिससे मरीज को बहुत कम समय में आराम मिलता है। . पूर्ण निर्माण विधि (Step-by-Step Manufacturing Method)इस जेनेटिक फॉर्मूले और नेज़ल स्प्रे को प्रयोगशाला (BSL-4 Lab) में तैयार करने की वैज्ञानिक विधि नीचे दी गई है:चरण 1: जेनेटिक कोड का अलगाव और रूपांतरण (Isolation & Reverse Transcription)सबसे पहले हंतावायरस के तीनों प्राकृतिक आरएनए खंडों (L, M, और S) को अलग किया जाता है।Reverse Transcriptase एंजाइम का उपयोग करके इस वायरस आरएनए (RNA) को cDNA (Complementary DNA) में बदला जाता है, ताकि इसके कोड को आसानी से बदला जा सके।चरण 2: कोड को उलटना और निष्क्रिय करना (Gene Splice & Inversion)CRISPR-Cas13 या विशिष्ट Restriction Enzymes (आणविक कैंची) की मदद से cDNA के उन हिस्सों को काटा जाता है जो बीमारी फैलाने और वायरस निर्माण के लिए जिम्मेदार हैं।काटे गए जेनेटिक अनुक्रम (Sequence) को उलट (Invert) दिया जाता है और DNA Ligase एंजाइम की मदद से वापस जोड़ दिया जाता है। अब यह कोड पूरी तरह हानिरहित हो जाता है। चरण 3: संशोधित आरएनए का निर्माण (Transcription)इस बदले हुए DNA से RNA Polymerase एंजाइम की मदद से वापस एक नया, संशोधित और निष्क्रिय आरएनए (Modified Inactive RNA Code) तैयार किया जाता है।चरण 4: लिपिड कवच का निर्माण (Lipid Nano-Encapsulation)तैयार किए गए निष्क्रिय जेनेटिक कोड को सुरक्षित रखने के लिए उसे लिपिड (वसा) के नैनोपार्टिकल्स के घोल में मिलाया जाता है। यह लिपिड कवच कोड को शरीर के एंजाइमों द्वारा नष्ट होने से बचाता है और कोशिकाओं के अंदर आसानी से प्रवेश करने में मदद करता है।चरण 5: नेज़ल स्प्रे फॉर्मूलेशन (Nasal Spray Formulation)इस लिपिड-कोडेड मिश्रण को एक स्टेराइल लिक्विड बेस (जैसे सेलाइन सोल्यूशन) में मिलाकर एक सटीक नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) की बोतल में पैक किया जाता है, जो उपयोग के लिए तैयार होता है। तकनीकी परिशिष्ट: H-GEN Spray की रासायनिक संरचना और आणविक सूत्र (Chemical Formulation)मुख्य अन्वेषक (Lead Innovator): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)दस्तावेज़ कोड: H-GEN/CHEM-v11. सक्रिय जेनेटिक घटक (Active Genetic Cargo)हंतावायरस के प्राकृतिक L, M, और S आरएनए (RNA) खंडों को काटने और निष्क्रिय करने के लिए तैयार किए गए कृत्रिम एंटीसेंस गाइड आरएनए (gRNA) की आणविक संरचना: [1] (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4661284/), [2] (https://microbenotes.com/hanta-virus/)संशोधित न्यूक्लियोटाइड चेन (Modified RNA Backbone): \(\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_{5}\text{O}_{7}\text{P}\) (Adenosine Phosphate Base), \(\text{C}_{9}\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{8}\text{P}\) (Cytidine Phosphate Base), \(\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_{5}\text{O}_{8}\text{P}\) (Guanosine Phosphate Base), और \(\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{14}\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{8}\text{P}\) (\(N^{1}\)-Methylpseudouridine).)रासायनिक प्रकृति: यह फॉस्फोडिएस्टर लिंकेज (Phosphodiester Linkage) के माध्यम से आपस में जुड़े न्यूक्लियोटाइड बहुलक (Polymers) हैं, जो नकारात्मक चार्ज (-ve Charge) वाले होते हैं। 2. लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल कवच की रासायनिक संरचना (Lipid Nanoparticle Sheath)संशोधित जेनेटिक कोड को सुरक्षित रूप से श्वसन नली (Respiratory Tract) के माध्यम से फेफड़ों में पहुँचाने के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल्स (LNPs) का रासायनिक मिश्रण और उनके सूत्र निम्नलिखित हैं: [1] ( )घटक का नाम (Component Name)रासायनिक भूमिका (Chemical Role)आणविक रासायनिक सूत्र (Chemical Formula)आयोजिनाइजेबल लिपिड (Ionizable Lipid - e.g., ALC-0315 / SM-102)यह जेनेटिक कोड के नकारात्मक चार्ज को न्यूट्रलाइज कर उसे कैप्सूल में बांधता है और कोशिका के भीतर प्रवेश कराता है।\(\text{C}_{48}\text{H}_{95}\text{NO}_{5}\)सहायक फॉस्फोलिपिड (Helper Phospholipid - DSPC)यह लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल (LNP) की बाहरी द्विसतह (Bilayer Structure) को मजबूती और स्थिरता प्रदान करता है।\(\text{C}_{44}\text{H}_{88}\text{NO}_{8}\text{P}\)स्ट्रक्चरल कोलेस्ट्रॉल (Cholesterol)यह कणों के लचीलेपन (Fluidity) को नियंत्रित करता है ताकि स्प्रे होते समय नैनोकण टूटे नहीं।\(\text{C}_{27}\text{H}_{46}\text{O}\)पेगिलेटेड लिपिड (PEG-Lipid - e.g., ALC-0159)यह घोल में लिपिड कणों को आपस में चिपकने (Aggregation) से रोकता है और दवा की शेल्फ-लाइफ बढ़ाता है।\(\text{C}_{31}\text{H}_{63}\text{O}_{2}\cdot(\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{4}\text{O})_{n}\) (जहाँ \(n \approx 45\)) 3. तरल बेस (Delivery Base Solution)स्प्रे को नाक की श्लेष्मा झिल्ली (Nasal Mucosa) के अनुकूल और जलन-रहित बनाने के लिए उपयोग होने वाला विलायक (Solvent Base):बफर्ड खारा पानी (Sterile Saline Base): \(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\) (शुद्ध आसुत जल) + \(\text{NaCl}\) (सोडियम क्लोराइड - 0.9% सामर्थ्य बनाए रखने के लिए, जो मानव शरीर के प्राकृतिक द्रवों के समान है)।पीएच नियामक (pH Regulator): \(\text{Na}_{2}\text{HPO}_{4}\) (सोडियम फॉस्फेट दिबासिक) और \(\text{KH}_{2}\text{PO}_{4}\) (पोटेशियम फॉस्फेट मोनोबासिक), जो घोल का pH 7.2 से 7.4 के बीच (हल्का क्षारीय) स्थिर रखते हैं। H-GEN SPRAY KI full_text_sections.abstract: वैज्ञानिक शोध प्रस्ताव: हंतावायरस के विरुद्ध रिवर्स जेनेटिक्स और लिपिड-आधारित नेज़ल स्प्रे तकनीकअवधारणा एवं लेखक: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)विषय: वायरोलॉजी एवं बायो-मेडिकल इंजीनियरिंग (Theoretical Concept)1. परिचय (Introduction)हंतावायरस (Hantavirus) एक गंभीर वैश्विक स्वास्थ्य संकट है, जो मुख्य रूप से मनुष्यों के श्वसन तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है। वर्तमान में इसके सटीक इलाज के लिए शोध जारी हैं। इस लेख में, लेखक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा हंतावायरस को निष्क्रिय करने और उसे शरीर के भीतर ही नष्ट करने के लिए एक त्रि-स्तरीय जेनेटिक और नैनो-पार्टिकल आधारित चिकित्सा प्रणाली का प्रस्ताव रखा गया है।2. मुख्य सिद्धांत: L, M, और S खंडों का विलोपन (Targeting L, M, S Segments)हंतावायरस का जीनोम तीन प्रमुख आरएनए (RNA) खंडों से बना होता है: L (Large) जो रेप्लिकेशन एंजाइम बनाता है, M (Medium) जो बाहरी ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन कवच तैयार करता है, और S (Small) जो न्यूक्लियोकैप्सिड प्रोटीन बनाता है।इस परिकल्पना के अनुसार, वायरस के इन तीनों प्राकृतिक खंडों के जेनेटिक कोड को उलट (Invert) या बदल दिया जाएगा। इससे वायरस अपनी प्रतिकृति (Photocopy) बनाने की क्षमता खो देगा और बीमारी फैलाने के लायक नहीं रहेगा। 3. आणविक कार्यप्रणाली और एंजाइम प्रक्रिया (Molecular Mechanism Flowchart)इस जेनेटिक बदलाव को अंजाम देने के लिए आधुनिक मॉलिक्यूलर बायोलॉजी के उपकरणों और एंजाइमों का उपयोग निम्नलिखित फ्लोचार्ट के अनुसार प्रस्तावित है:[Virus RNA] ➔ (Reverse Transcriptase) ➔ [cDNA] ➔ (CRISPR/Restriction Enzymes) ➔ [Invert/Change Code] ➔ (RNA Polymerase) ➔ [Modified Inactive Virus] स्टेप 1 (Reverse Transcriptase): सबसे पहले हंतावायरस के प्राकृतिक RNA को 'रिवर्स ट्रांसक्रिप्टेज' एंजाइम की मदद से cDNA (Complementary DNA) में बदला जाएगा, ताकि लैब में इस पर काम करना आसान हो सके।स्टेप 2 (CRISPR/Restriction Enzymes): इसके बाद मॉलिक्यूलर कैंची (CRISPR-Cas या Restriction Enzymes) का उपयोग करके L, M, और S खंडों के विशिष्ट हिस्सों को काटा जाएगा।स्टेप 3 (Invert/Change Code): कटे हुए जेनेटिक कोड के अनुक्रम (Sequence) को उलट दिया जाएगा ताकि वायरस का मूल सिस्टम ब्लॉक हो जाए।स्टेप 4 (RNA Polymerase): अंत में, 'आरएनए पॉलीमरेज' एंजाइम द्वारा इस बदले हुए DNA से पुनः एक निष्क्रिय, हानिरहित वायरस (Modified Inactive Virus) तैयार किया जाएगा। 4. डिलीवरी माध्यम: लिपिड नैनोपार्टिकल नेज़ल स्प्रे (Delivery System)इस संशोधित निष्क्रिय कोड को मानव शरीर में सुरक्षित रूप से पहुँचाने के लिए लेखक ने नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) का माध्यम चुना है।ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन कवच और लिपिड: इस कोड को वसा (Lipid) के एक सुरक्षात्मक कवच (Lipid Nanoparticle) में लपेटा जाएगा।यह स्प्रे नाक के रास्ते सीधे फेफड़ों और श्वसन नली (Respiratory Tract) तक पहुँचेगा, जो हंतावायरस का मुख्य हमला क्षेत्र है। शरीर में जाकर यह एक एंटीबॉडी की तरह काम करेगा और असली वायरस को आगे बढ़ने से रोक देगा। वैज्ञानिक शोध लेख: हंतावायरस रोधी जेनेटिक थेरेपी और लिपिड नेज़ल स्प्रे (H-GEN Spray)मुख्य आविष्कारक (Lead Innovator): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat)क्षेत्र: वायरोलॉजी, मॉलिक्यूलर बायोलॉजी एवं नैनो-मेडिसिन (सैद्धांतिक मॉडल)1. प्रस्तावना (Introduction)हंतावायरस (Hantavirus) मुख्य रूप से फेफड़ों और श्वसन प्रणाली पर हमला करता है, जिससे हंतावायरस पल्मोनरी सिंड्रोम (HPS) जैसी जानलेवा बीमारियां होती हैं। वर्तमान में इसका कोई सटीक इलाज उपलब्ध नहीं है। आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा तैयार यह शोध लेख एक ऐसी अत्याधुनिक चिकित्सा पद्धति का प्रस्ताव करता है, जो वायरस के जेनेटिक कोड (L, M, S खंडों) को निष्क्रिय कर, एक लिपिड-आधारित नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) के माध्यम से सीधे फेफड़ों तक दवा पहुँचाती है। 2. इस आविष्कार के मुख्य फायदे और लाभ (Key Advantages & Benefits)बंटी कुमावत के इस फॉर्मूले के पारंपरिक दवाओं और टीकों की तुलना में निम्नलिखित बड़े फायदे हैं:सटीक निशाना (Targeted Delivery): हंतावायरस सीधे सांस की नली और फेफड़ों को प्रभावित करता है। यह फॉर्मूला नेज़ल स्प्रे के माध्यम से सीधे संक्रमित क्षेत्र (Target Organ) पर पहुँचता है, जिससे दवा पूरे शरीर में फैलने के बजाय सीधे फेफड़ों में काम शुरू कर देती है।वायरस की फोटोकॉपी (Replication) पर पूर्ण रोक: वायरस के L खंड को ब्लॉक करने के कारण वायरस शरीर की कोशिकाओं के अंदर अपनी संख्या (Replication) नहीं बढ़ा पाता। संख्या न बढ़ने से बीमारी तुरंत रुक जाती है।भविष्य के म्यूटेशन से सुरक्षा: यह थेरेपी वायरस के किसी एक हिस्से पर नहीं, बल्कि उसके तीनों बुनियादी खंडों (L, M, S) पर एक साथ हमला करती है। यदि वायरस अपना रूप बदलता (Mutate होता) भी है, तो भी वह इस थेरेपी से बच नहीं सकता।शारीरिक सुरक्षा और कम साइड इफेक्ट्स: इसमें उपयोग किया जाने वाला बाहरी आवरण प्राकृतिक लिपिड (वसा) का है, जिसे मानव शरीर आसानी से स्वीकार कर लेता है। इससे पारंपरिक दवाओं की तरह शरीर के अन्य अंगों (जैसे लिवर या किडनी) पर कोई दुष्प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।तीव्र प्रतिरक्षा (Fast-Acting Immunity): यह स्प्रे शरीर में जाते ही एंटीबॉडीज की तरह सक्रिय रूप से असली वायरस को ढूंढकर उसे काटना शुरू कर देता है, जिससे मरीज को बहुत कम समय में आराम मिलता है। . पूर्ण निर्माण विधि (Step-by-Step Manufacturing Method)इस जेनेटिक फॉर्मूले और नेज़ल स्प्रे को प्रयोगशाला (BSL-4 Lab) में तैयार करने की वैज्ञानिक विधि नीचे दी गई है:चरण 1: जेनेटिक कोड का अलगाव और रूपांतरण (Isolation & Reverse Transcription)सबसे पहले हंतावायरस के तीनों प्राकृतिक आरएनए खंडों (L, M, और S) को अलग किया जाता है।Reverse Transcriptase एंजाइम का उपयोग करके इस वायरस आरएनए (RNA) को cDNA (Complementary DNA) में बदला जाता है, ताकि इसके कोड को आसानी से बदला जा सके।चरण 2: कोड को उलटना और निष्क्रिय करना (Gene Splice & Inversion)CRISPR-Cas13 या विशिष्ट Restriction Enzymes (आणविक कैंची) की मदद से cDNA के उन हिस्सों को काटा जाता है जो बीमारी फैलाने और वायरस निर्माण के लिए जिम्मेदार हैं।काटे गए जेनेटिक अनुक्रम RNA Polymerase एंजाइम की मदद से वापस एक नया, संशोधित और निष्क्रिय आरएनए (Modified Inactive RNA Code) तैयार किया जाता है।चरण 4: लिपिड कवच का निर्माण (Lipid Nano-Encapsulation)तैयार किए गए निष्क्रिय करने में मदद करता है।चरण 5: नेज़ल स्प्रे फॉर्मूलेशन (Nasal Spray Formulation)इस लिपिड-कोडेड मिश्रण को एक स्टेराइल लिक्विड बेस (जैसे सेलाइन सोल्यूशन) में मिलाकर एक सटीक नेज़ल स्प्रे (Nasal Spray) की analysis.background: The paper proposes a theoretical genetic therapy to inactivate hantavirus by targeting its L, M, and S RNA segments, addressing a global health crisis with no current cure.
analysis.methods: It outlines a multi‑step laboratory protocol: reverse transcription of viral RNA to cDNA, CRISPR or restriction enzyme editing to invert or alter the L, M, S segments, transcription back to modified RNA, lipid nanoparticle encapsulation, and formulation into a nasal spray base.
analysis.results: No experimental results are reported; the work remains a conceptual design.
analysis.contribution: It offers a novel, targeted delivery concept that could bypass traditional vaccine or antiviral limitations by directly neutralizing viral replication in the respiratory tract.
analysis.limitations: The study is limited to a theoretical framework with no empirical data; the evidence is from an abstract only.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The paper proposes a theoretical genetic therapy to inactivate hantavirus by targeting its L, M, and S RNA segments, addressing a global health crisis with no current cure. Methods: It outlines a multi‑step laboratory protocol: reverse transcription of viral RNA to cDNA, CRISPR or restriction enzyme editing to invert or alter the L, M, S segments, transcription back to modified RNA, lipid nanoparticle encapsulation, and formulation into a nasal spray base. Results: No experimental results are reported; the work remains a conceptual design. Contribution: It offers a novel, targeted delivery concept that could bypass traditional vaccine or antiviral limitations by directly neutralizing viral replication in the respiratory tract. Limitations: The study is limited to a theoretical framework with no empirical data; the evidence is from an abstract only.

papers.title_zh: H-GEN Spray:理论基因疗法与基于脂质纳米颗粒的鼻腔递送系统用于汉坦病毒消除

analysis_zh.background: 本文提出一种理论性的基因疗法,通过靶向其 L、M、S RNA 片段来灭活 汉坦病毒,以应对目前尚无治愈方法的全球健康危机。
analysis_zh.methods: 其概述了多步实验室流程:将病毒 RNA 逆转录为 cDNA,利用 CRISPR 或限制性酶编辑逆转或改变 L、M、S 片段,随后转录回改造后的 RNA,脂质纳米颗粒包封,并制成鼻喷剂基质。
analysis_zh.results: 未报告实验结果;该工作仍为概念设计。

papers.title: The rationale for ophthalmic vigilance during the 2026 Hantavirus outbreak.
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious disease preparedness has traditionally focused on emergency medicine, infectious disease, and critical care specialists. However, the ophthalmologist is not insulated from emerging infectious disease. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak highlights why ophthalmologists should also be incorporated into outbreak surveillance and response. Throughout history, ophthalmologists have played an important role in identifying infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. Yet, this role depends on a clear understanding of a pathogen’s ophthalmic phenotype. Despite growing attention surrounding the current Andes virus outbreak, the ocular manifestations of this pathogen remain largely undefined. This knowledge gap presents both an opportunity and a responsibility for ophthalmologists to systematically characterise ocular involvement and contribute to emerging infectious disease surveillance. Herein, we review the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection and contend that ophthalmologists have a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the current outbreak.

Deaner ]]]2,3✉ © The Author(s) 2026 Eye; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41433-026-04848-9 Emerging infectious disease preparedness has traditionally focused on emergency medicine, infectious disease, and critical care specialists. However, the ophthalmologist is not insulated from emerging infectious disease. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak highlights why ophthalmologists should also be incorporated into outbreak surveillance and response. Throughout history, ophthal­ mologists have played an important role in identifying infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. Yet, this role depends on a clear understanding of a pathogen’s ophthalmic phenotype. Despite growing attention surrounding the current Andes virus outbreak, the ocular manifestations of this pathogen remain largely undefined. This knowledge gap presents both an opportunity and a responsibility for ophthalmologists to system­ atically characterise ocular involvement and contribute to emerging infectious disease surveillance. Herein, we review the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection and contend that ophthalmologists have a critical role in defining the ocular phenotype of Andes virus during the current outbreak. The Andes strain of Hantavirus was recently documented aboard an international vessel. In April 2026, passengers and crew aboard the MV Hondius, began developing severe respiratory illness during an itinerary across the South Atlantic. The World Health Organization was notified on May 2, 2026, and Andes virus was confirmed as the causative pathogen on May 5 [1]. As of late- May 2026, 13 confirmed or probable cases and 3 deaths had been reported across multiple countries, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) monitoring several individuals across multiple US states [2]. Although the overall public health risk in the United States remains low, the CDC has issued a Health Alert Network advisory emphasising heightened clinical vigilance. Hantaviruses (family Hantaviridae) are enveloped, single- stranded, negative-sense RNA viruses transmitted primarily through aerosolisation of infected rodent excrement, causing two principal syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) from New World hantaviruses including Sin Nombre and Andes viruses, and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) from Old World hantaviruses such as Puumala, Hantaan, and Seoul viruses. Andes virus is the only hantavirus with recently confirmed person-to-person transmission, typically via respiratory secretions during prolonged close contact with a symptomatic individual [3]. The ophthalmic literature on hantavirus is dominated by Puumala virus, which causes nephropathia epidemica (NE), a generally mild to moderate, renal-predominant form of HFRS. In the largest prospective ophthalmic series to date, Hautala et al. examined 92 eyes of 46 serologically confirmed NE patients and found that 70% reported ocular symptoms during acute illness, with decreased IOP in 88%, reduced visual acuity in 87%, conjunctival chemosis in 87%, crystalline lens thickening in 82%, a myopic shift in 78%, anterior chamber shallowing in 64%, and shortened vitreous length in 52% [4]. All anterior segment changes resolved fully with systemic recovery. Transient myopia is the hallmark finding, occasionally exceeding −4.0 diopters [5]. External findings include periorbital oedema, conjunctival injec­ tion, and subconjunctival haemorrhage [4–6]. Posterior findings are less frequent but include retinal haemorrhages, macular oedema, retinal whitening near the optic disc, and a self-limiting posterior necrotising retinitis, with neuro-ophthalmic manifesta­ tions possible when CNS complications such as hypophyseal haemorrhage occur [5]. Although ocular manifestations of Puumala strain of hantavirus infection are well described, virtually no ophthalmic data exist for Andes virus, the pathogen responsible for the current outbreak. This distinction is critical because existing ophthalmic knowledge is derived from a different virus, a different clinical syndrome, and a substantially different severity spectrum. What we do know is that in contrast to the Puumala virus, the systemic manifestations of the Andes virus causes HPS, a fulminant cardiopulmonary illness in which patients progress rapidly to respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and in severe cases extracorporeal support [7]. To date, no ophthalmic evaluation of HPS patients has been published. This gap in knowledge has practical consequences. Clinically, this means that the pattern of presentation that ophthalmologists may be tasked to recognise is extrapolated from a population that differs in virus, syndrome severity, and clinical state. The existing literature on the Puumala virus may be used to prompt suspicion (i.e., a febrile patient with bilateral unexplained myopic shift should raise the possibility of hantavirus), but it cannot yet tell ophthalmologists what Andes virus ocular disease looks like beyond that. The current outbreak represents not only a clinical challenge but also a scientific opportunity. For ophthalmologists, this means that every HPS patient managed at a US referral centre 1Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, USA. 2Retina Service, Wills Eye Hospital, Philadelphia, PA, USA. 3Sidney Kimmel Medical College of Thomas Jefferson University, Philadelphia, PA, USA. ✉email: jdeaner@midatlanticretina.com Received: 20 July 2026 Revised: 22 July 2026 Accepted: 1 September 2026 1234567890();,: during the current outbreak who is well enough to undergo ophthalmic evaluation represents an opportunity to generate evidence that does not yet exist. A standardised assessment, documented and reported in the literature, would begin to answer a question that the existing literature cannot. Importantly, ophthalmologists should examine patients with known or suspected hantavirus using correct transmission-based precautions. Unlike other hantaviruses, Andes virus has documen­ ted person-to-person transmission via respiratory secretions, a characteristic with no known analogue among other hantaviruses. For ophthalmologists, this distinction is particularly relevant because slit-lamp examination requires prolonged face-to-face proximity. Consequently, infection-control preparedness should be considered. The CDC recommends airborne infection isolation with gown, gloves, eye protection, and an N95 or higher-level respirator for any patient with confirmed or suspected infection [2]. Historically, ophthalmologists have contributed immensely to the recognition and characterisation of systemic infectious diseases through their ocular manifestations. From syphilis and tuberculosis to more recent outbreaks involving Zika virus, Mpox, and COVID-19, ocular findings have occasionally provided diagnostic clues, insight into disease pathogenesis, and opportu­ nities for longitudinal monitoring. The Andes virus should be viewed within this broader framework. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak carries with it a powerful lesson. We as ophthalmologists are not peripheral observers during emerging infectious disease events. We contribute to surveillance, diagnosis, characterisation of novel ocular manifestations, and implementation of appropriate infection-control practices. As the outbreak evolves, systematic ophthalmic evaluation of affected patients may help close a major knowledge gap regarding the ocular manifestations of the Hantavirus Andes strain infection. analysis.methods: The authors conducted a narrative review of the available evidence regarding ocular involvement in hantavirus infection to define the ophthalmic phenotype of Andes virus.
analysis.results: The ocular manifestations of Andes virus remain largely undefined, and to date no ophthalmic evaluation of HPS patients caused by Andes virus has been published.
analysis.contribution: The review identifies an opportunity and responsibility for ophthalmologists to systematically characterize ocular involvement and contribute to outbreak surveillance and response.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Emerging infectious disease preparedness has traditionally focused on emergency, infectious disease, and critical care specialists, yet ophthalmologists are also at risk, as shown by the 2026 Andes virus outbreak. Methods: The authors performed a narrative review of existing literature on ocular involvement in hantavirus infection. Results: Ocular manifestations of Andes virus remain largely undefined, and no ophthalmic evaluation of HPS patients has been published. Contribution: The review highlights an opportunity and responsibility for ophthalmologists to characterize ocular findings and aid surveillance. Limitations: Findings are constrained by the lack of primary ophthalmic data on Andes virus and reliance on indirect evidence from other hantavirus strains.

analysis_zh.contribution: 本综述指出眼科医生有机会和责任系统性地表征眼部受累,并为疫情监测与应对做出贡献。

papers.title: Increasing spatial scale of analysis weakens and can mask the dilution effect for hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Despite its major implications for biodiversity conservation and public health, the generality of a protective effect of biodiversity on zoonotic pathogen transmission (i.e., the dilution effect) remains strongly debated. This controversy may partly arise from the diversity of analytical approaches used, but also from the spatial scales at which studies are conducted. Here, we explicitly test whether increasing the spatial scale of analysis affects the detection of the relationship between hantavirus infection prevalence and rodent species richness, using a global dataset spanning multiple regions. Although the association between species richness and infection prevalence remains negative across all spatial scales, we show that the magnitude of the dilution effect progressively weakens as spatial aggregation increases and can become statistically non-significant at coarse spatial resolutions. These results, which are consistent across world regions, indicate that the dilution effect is likely a general feature of hantavirus-rodent systems, but that its empirical detection is highly sensitive to the spatial scale of analysis. Our findings highlight how large-scale spatial aggregation can mask underlying ecological processes and emphasize the need to carefully match spatial scale to the biological mechanisms under investigation when testing biodiversity-disease relationships. Finally, we discuss the ecological and methodological mechanisms that may obscure dilution effects and outline why scale-explicit approaches are essential for robust inference in biodiversity-disease research.

PLOS Global Public Health | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgph.0007045 September 8, 2026 2 / 11 Introduction In the mid-twentieth century, the widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics substan­ tially reduced the burden of many infectious diseases and contributed to optimism about their future control [1]. However, this optimism has since been tempered by the steadily increasing frequency of emerging infections, illustrated by the examples of zoonotic diseases like Ebola virus in West Africa, Zika virus in South America, or, more recently the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) [2,3]. Moreover, these new threats seem to be closely linked to environmental issues such as climate change, land-use change and forest loss, because most of these emerging pathogens originate from wildlife [2]. To this extent, the potential link between the increased transmission of zoonotic pathogens and the reduction of vertebrate biodiversity clearly calls for investigating the possibility of using biodiversity conservation strategies as a public health oppor­ tunity [4–7]. Currently, much research focuses on the dilution effect theory, which suggests that a greater species richness within vertebrate communities (hereafter called hosts) can reduce (dilute) pathogen transmission [8,9] through several mech­ anisms [10]. First, the addition of non-competent host species, i.e., weakly or not at all involved in pathogen transmission within the ecosystem can theoretically reduce transmission of some pathogen species by decreasing contacts among competent host species [11]. However, a dilution effect can also be detected if the abundance of a species that strongly contributes to pathogen transmission, i.e., a highly com­ petent host, negatively correlates with host species richness [12]. It is nevertheless important to point out that a greater species richness within host communities could also increase pathogen prevalence, i.e., creating an amplification effect, and may be associated with enhanced risk of pathogen emergence [9]. Such amplification could also be associated with increases in pathogen richness in parallel with host species diversity [13]. The generality of dilution and amplification effects therefore remains strongly debated [9]. Empirical evidence suggests that the direction and strength of biodiversity-disease relationships can depend on multiple factors, including the composition and complexity of the vertebrate host communities [14–17]. Dilution and amplification processes may even occur concurrently within the same host-pathogen system [18]. As a result, it remains unclear under which ecological contexts dilution or amplification effects should be expected, and which mechanisms primarily drive these contrasting outcomes. Part of this ongoing debate may stem from methodological heterogeneity among studies, particularly differences in spatial scale, ecosystem type, and metrics used to quantify pathogen transmission [19–23]. Spatial scale is especially critical as ecological processes influencing host community structure and pathogen transmission occur at different spatial scales. Consequently, analyses conducted at mismatched or overly coarse spatial resolutions may obscure underlying biodiversity-disease relationships, contributing to apparently contrasting empirical results. PLOS Global Public Health | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgph.0007045 September 8, 2026 3 / 11 In this study, we test whether the relationship between host species richness and pathogen prevalence—negative under a dilution effect or positive under an amplification effect—depends on the spatial scale at which it is assessed. Beyond the direction of this relationship, our central focus is on its magnitude, i.e., on how strongly an additional rodent species reduces hantavirus prevalence, and on whether that magnitude is preserved as the unit of analysis is coarsened. Using a global scale-explicit re-analysis of a compiled dataset of hantavirus prevalence across rodent host communities, we quantify how systematic changes in the spatial extent of study areas modify the inferred relationship between biodi­ versity and pathogen prevalence. We specifically examine whether increasing spatial aggregation alters both the strength and the statistical detectability of biodiversity–disease relationships. Finally, we discuss the ecological and methodolog­ ical mechanisms that may obscure biodiversity–disease relationships and emphasize the need to adopt scale-explicit approaches, and to extend this scale-explicit framework to other host–pathogen systems. Materials and methods Biological model Orthohantaviruses (enveloped, single-stranded, negative sense, RNA viruses belonging to the family Hantaviridae) constitute a particularly suitable biological model to characterise the effect of spatial scale on dilution/amplification effect. Hantaviruses are transmitted by various rodent species of the superfamily Muroidea in Europe, Asia, and the Americas [25], which are habitat generalists, geographically widespread, and locally highly abundant, making them well suited for large-scale comparative analyses. Moreover, despite several hantaviruses that tend to use several hosts [26], hantavi­ ruses tend nevertheless to be “specialist”, i.e., associated with only one given small-mammal species (especially rodents, shrews, moles, and bats) For example, Puumala virus (PUUV) in Europe is essentially restricted to the bank vole Myodes glareolus, Sin Nombre virus (SNV) in North America is primarily carried by the deer mouse Peromyscus maniculatus, and Andes virus in southern South America is associated with the long-tailed pygmy rice rat Oligoryzomys longicaudatus. By contrast, Seoul virus (SEOV), the dominant hantavirus genotype in our Asian dataset, infects several commensal Rattus species, and Tula virus (TULV) in Europe circulates across multiple Microtus voles, so that some hantaviruses fit a “multi- host” pattern. The richness term we model here is total rodent species richness in the cell, rather than the richness of competent reservoirs only, because for most non-reservoir species hantavirus competence has not been quantitatively assessed in the literature compiled by Milholland et al. [26,27]; we revisit this point in the Discussion [28]. This host adap­ tation pattern yields a large variability in host competence within rodent communities. In this context, the dilution effect has been observed several times for these hantaviruses, being especially evident when host species richness is high with an associated decrease in relative abundance of the most susceptible host species [29,30]. Moreover, hantaviruses represent a significant threat to human health. Transmission to humans occurs mainly via inhalation of aerosolized virus particles from infected rodent excreta or through direct contact with infected hosts, and can cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (mainly in Asia and Europe) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (mainly in the Americas) [31]. Thus, identifying the ecological determinants of the relationship between hantavirus prevalence and host species richness is crucial for understanding and preventing zoonotic disease risk in human populations. Dataset The dataset used in this study is described by Milholland et al. [26,27]. In brief, this dataset comes from an extensive survey of the literature between 1971–2015 and comprises a global compilation of wild rodent species and their docu­ mented associations with hantaviruses. For each study, the dataset includes the number of individuals testing positive or negative for specific hantavirus species based on direct detection of viral genetic material (RNA). Accordingly, only host-virus associations confirmed by RT-PCR were retained. Although this molecular approach likely underestimates total host exposure compared to serology-based studies, it ensures a high specificity of host-virus associations by excluding PLOS Global Public Health | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgph.0007045 September 8, 2026 4 / 11 serologic records in which specific hantavirus genotypes cannot be reliably identified. Therefore, data for each locality of the field study extracted involves sampling date, rodent species sampled, number of each hantavirus genotype iden­ tified within each rodent species, and total sample size for each rodent species. In total, the dataset contains exploitable data for three regions (North America, Asia, and Europe), encompassing 154 rodent species, 17,893 rodent individuals screened by RT-PCR (1,575 positives), and 19 hantavirus genotypes. A region-by-region breakdown of sampling effort, host species (including region-endemic species that tested positive), dominant hantavirus genotypes and main reservoir hosts is provided in S1 and S2 Tables. Statistical aggregation Spatial aggregation was performed using an equal-area hexagonal grid to ensure comparability of spatial units across lat­ itudes. This avoids geometric distortions inherent to latitude–longitude grids defined in degrees, in which cell area varies with latitude, and provides a consistent definition of spatial scale. Hexagons were generated separately for each region in a Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area (LAEA) projection centered on the mean longitude and latitude of that region’s sampling sites, in order to preserve cell area while minimising local distortion. Twelve grain sizes were evaluated, defined by the hexagon “diameter” (the distance between opposite vertices): 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 and 800 km. These grains span roughly two orders of magnitude in area, from sub-landscape (≈10 km) to sub-continental (≈800 km), and were chosen because they bracket the spatial extents at which biotic interactions among rodent hosts and large- scale climatic constraints respectively dominate community assembly. For each region and each grain, only cells contain­ ing at least two rodent species and a non-zero sampling effort (N > 0) were retained in the analysis. Fig 1 displays the raw, unaggregated sampling sites (i.e., point coordinates from the source dataset, with no spatial pooling); aggregation into hexagonal cells was applied only to the statistical analysis underlying Fig 2. Spatial grain was systematically increased by varying hexagonal cell size, thereby pooling progressively larger areas while maintaining constant cell area within each resolution. This approach allows spatial scale to be interpreted unambigu­ ously in terms of area rather than angular distance. Fig 1. The size of the circles increases with the rodent species richness measured and the color represents the prevalence observed. This approach accounts for the bounded nature of prevalence data and for heterogeneity in sampling effort among spatial units. To accommodate potential overdispersion arising from aggregation across multiple host species and study sites, a quasi-binomial variance was specified whenever the residual deviance dispersion exceeded 1.5, so that standard errors and p-values are inflated to account for extra-binomial variability. A negative β1 indicates a dilution effect, a positive β1 an amplification effect. BR and AA are co-last authors on this work. * ana.vigueras09@gmail.com Abstract Despite its major implications for biodiversity conservation and public health, the gen­ erality of a protective effect of biodiversity on zoonotic pathogen transmission (i.e., the dilution effect) remains strongly debated. This controversy may partly arise from the diversity of analytical approaches used, but also from the spatial scales at which studies are conducted. Here, we explicitly test whether increasing the spatial scale of analysis affects the detection of the relationship between hantavirus infection preva­ lence and rodent species richness, using a global dataset spanning multiple regions. Although the association between species richness and infection prevalence remains negative across all spatial scales, we show that the magnitude of the dilution effect progressively weakens as spatial aggregation increases and can become statistically non-significant at coarse spatial resolutions. These results, which are consistent across world regions, indicate that the dilution effect is likely a general feature of hantavirus–rodent systems, but that its empirical detection is highly sensitive to the spatial scale of analysis. Our findings highlight how large-scale spatial aggregation can mask underlying ecological processes and emphasize the need to carefully match spatial scale to the biological mechanisms under investigation when testing biodiversity–disease relationships. Finally, we discuss the ecological and method­ ological mechanisms that may obscure dilution effects and outline why scale-explicit approaches are essential for robust inference in biodiversity-disease research. PLOS Global Public Health | https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgph.0007045 September 8, 2026 2 / 11 Introduction In the mid-twentieth century, the widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics substan­ tially reduced the burden of many infectious diseases and contributed to optimism about their future control [1]. However, this optimism has since been tempered by the steadily increasing frequency of emerging infections, illustrated by the examples of zoonotic diseases like Ebola virus in West Africa, Zika virus in South America, or, more recently the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) [2,3]. Moreover, these new threats seem to be closely linked to environmental issues such as climate change, land-use change and forest loss, because most of these emerging pathogens originate from wildlife [2]. To this extent, the potential link between the increased transmission of zoonotic pathogens and the reduction of vertebrate biodiversity clearly calls for investigating the possibility of using biodiversity conservation strategies as a public health oppor­ tunity [4–7]. Currently, much research focuses on the dilution effect theory, which suggests that a greater species richness within vertebrate communities (hereafter called hosts) can reduce (dilute) pathogen transmission [8,9] through several mech­ anisms [10]. First, the addition of non-competent host species, i.e., weakly or not at all involved in pathogen transmission within the ecosystem can theoretically reduce transmission of some pathogen species by decreasing contacts among competent host species [11]. However, a dilution effect can also be detected if the abundance of a species that strongly contributes to pathogen transmission, i.e., a highly com­ petent host, negatively correlates with host species richness [12]. It is nevertheless important to point out that a greater species richness within host communities could also increase pathogen prevalence, i.e., creating an amplification effect, and may be associated with enhanced risk of pathogen emergence [9]. Such amplification could also be associated with increases in pathogen richness in parallel with host species diversity [13]. The generality of dilution and amplification effects therefore remains strongly debated [9]. Empirical evidence suggests that the direction and strength of biodiversity-disease relationships can depend on multiple factors, including the composition and complexity of the vertebrate host communities [14–17]. Dilution and amplification processes may even occur concurrently within the same host-pathogen system [18]. As a result, it remains unclear under which ecological contexts dilution or amplification effects should be expected, and which mechanisms primarily drive these contrasting outcomes. Part of this ongoing debate may stem from methodological heterogeneity among studies, particularly differences in spatial scale, ecosystem type, and metrics used to quantify pathogen transmission [19–23]. Spatial scale is especially critical as ecological processes influencing host community structure and pathogen transmission occur at different spatial scales. Consequently, analyses conducted at mismatched or overly coarse spatial resolutions may obscure underlying biodiversity-disease relationships, contributing to apparently contrasting empirical results. papers.title: Emerging Global Health Challenges: Which Poses a Greater Threat, Ebola Virus or Hantavirus?
papers.abstract: The world is experiencing more epidemics today than at any point in recent history, yet global readiness to respond is steadily slipping backwards. Pandemic risks, unstable geopolitics, and rapidly changing ecosystems have begun to outpace the world’s ability to prepare, creating conditions where future outbreaks may become far harder to manage (Global Preparedness Monitoring Board, 2026). As the global health system weakens, emerging viruses such as Ebola and hantavirus are appearing more frequently and with greater severity; from Ebola surging in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to hantavirus emerging unexpectedly on international cruise ships. In this rising landscape of vulnerability, which of these threats poses the greater global risk? To determine which virus poses the greater global risk, it is essential to examine how each behaves within a world that is increasingly unprepared for new outbreaks. Ebola typically enters human populations through contact with infected animals and then spreads efficiently through human-to-human transmission. Hantavirus, by contrast, is primarily transmitted from infected rodents to humans, with human-to-human spread occurring far less frequently (WHO, 2026) (WHO, 2025). Although both viruses are severe and potentially fatal, Ebola’s high transmissibility and mortality give it a clearer global threat profile, while hantavirus presents a different challenge: its symptoms often resemble mild illnesses, leading to delayed diagnosis and unpredictable detection patterns (BBC World Service, 2012). While Ebola and hantavirus differ in their transmission dynamics, both are classic examples of zoonotic diseases that underscore the importance of the One Health approach. Human encroachment into wildlife habitats, deforestation, agricultural expansion, biodiversity loss, and climate change continue to increase interactions between humans, wildlife, and animal reservoirs. These environmental changes facilitate the emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases, making future spillover events increasingly likely. Consequently, strengthening collaboration among public health, veterinary, environmental, and wildlife sectors should become a central component of global preparedness strategies rather than a reactive response once outbreaks occur. Another important lesson from both Ebola and hantavirus outbreaks is that preparedness cannot be measured solely by the availability of vaccines or clinical treatment. Robust surveillance systems, rapid laboratory diagnosis, effective risk communication, trained public health personnel, and cross-border information sharing are equally critical. Many countries continue to struggle with fragmented surveillance systems and inadequate laboratory capacity, resulting in delayed outbreak detection and response. Investing in preparedness before outbreaks occur remains substantially more cost-effective than responding after epidemics have already spread. Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), a severe form of Ebola, is currently affecting communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The virus is believed to originate from non-human primates or bats, and its rapid evolution raises growing concern. With no approved vaccines or specific treatments available, control efforts rely entirely on early case detection, isolation, and supportive care (WHO, 2026). Comparatively, the recent cruise ship–linked hantavirus outbreak was alarming because it travelled through 32 countries within a week, demonstrating how quickly even a rodent-borne virus can cross borders. However, WHO’s assessment indicates that the overall global risk remains relatively low: the Andes virus; the only hantavirus strain capable of human-to-human transmission, requires close and prolonged contact for spread. The danger of Hanta virus lies in delayed diagnoses (WHO, 2026). The question is not simply which virus poses more risk, but whether the world is prepared for what comes next? Both outbreaks could have been contained more effectively with stronger surveillance and preparedness systems, yet global capacity continues to erode, making timely public health responses increasingly difficult. Budget constraints have already forced major cutbacks, including a reduction in the WHO’s operating budget following the U.S. withdrawal, limiting the organisation’s ability to support outbreak response, early detection, and rapid containment (France 24, 2025). This decline in global readiness leaves the world increasingly vulnerable, regardless of whether the next threat emerges from Ebola, hantavirus, or an entirely new pathogen. Strengthening surveillance systems, investing in One Health approaches, and restoring sustainable global health financing should therefore become urgent international priorities before the next epidemic emerges.

papers.title: Generation and Characterization of the Human Anti-HTNV Antibody KJJ4
papers.abstract: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is the predominant causative agent of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in China, yet no specific antiviral therapy is currently available. Neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) represent a promising strategy, but most existing anti-HTNV NAbs are heterologous and carry immunogenicity risks. Here, two fully human antibodies from a previously established human anti-HTNV phage display library were generated and characterized. KJJ3, a VL-VL tandem antibody derived from clone 3–12, showed weak binding to inactivated HTNV and minimal neutralizing activity (IC50 = 27.12 μg/mL). However, KJJ4, an engineered IgG4 antibody derived from clone 4–19 and carrying the S108P hinge mutation to prevent Fab-arm exchange, bound inactivated HTNV antigen and recombinant glycoprotein Gn (residues 19–371) in a dose-dependent manner, with only weak binding to Gc. Surface plasmon resonance yielded an association rate constant of 4.70 × 103 M−1s−1, a dissociation rate constant of 3.06 × 10−3 s−1, and an equilibrium dissociation constant of 650 nM for monomeric Gn19–371. In a Vero E6 focus-reduction microneutralization assay, KJJ4 neutralized HTNV in vitro with an IC50 of 2.879 μg/mL. These data establish KJJ4 as a fully human anti-HTNV antibody with experimentally defined in vitro binding and neutralizing activity, warranting further evaluation in animal models of HTNV infection.

analysis.background: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is the predominant cause of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in China and no specific antiviral therapy exists (A1).
analysis.methods: Two fully human antibodies were generated from a human anti‑HTNV phage‑display library (A3); KJJ4 was engineered as an IgG4 with an S108P hinge mutation (A5); binding to inactivated HTNV, recombinant Gn (residues 19–371) and Gc was assessed dose‑dependently, and kinetic parameters were measured by surface plasmon resonance (A6); neutralizing activity was evaluated in a Vero E6 focus‑reduction microneutralization assay (A7).
analysis.results: KJJ3 displayed weak binding and minimal neutralization (IC50 = 27.12 µg/mL) (A4); KJJ4 bound Gn with an equilibrium dissociation constant of ~650 nM and weakly to Gc (A5, A6); in vitro KJJ4 neutralized HTNV with an IC50 of 2.879 µg/mL (A7).
analysis.contribution: The study establishes KJJ4 as a fully human anti‑HTNV antibody with experimentally defined in‑vitro binding and neutralizing activity, supporting further pre‑clinical evaluation (A8).
analysis.limitations: Data are limited to in‑vitro assays; no animal‑model or clinical evaluation is reported, and only abstract information is available (A8).

analysis.summary_en: Background: HTNV causes HFRS in China and lacks specific antivirals. Methods: Human antibodies were derived from a phage‑display library; KJJ4 was engineered as IgG4 with S108P hinge, binding to Gn measured by SPR, and neutralization tested in Vero E6 microneutralization assay. Results: KJJ3 showed weak activity (IC50 = 27.12 µg/mL); KJJ4 bound Gn (Kd ≈ 650 nM) and neutralized HTNV in vitro (IC50 = 2.879 µg/mL). Contribution: Demonstrates a fully human anti‑HTNV antibody with defined in‑vitro activity, warranting further pre‑clinical work. Limitations: Findings are restricted to in‑vitro data; no animal or clinical studies are presented; abstract only.

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantavirus Infection: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Molecular What-If Simulations
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, together responsible for more than 200,000 cases annually, but no specific antiviral therapy is approved. We developed a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptomic analysis of Hantaan virus-infected human umbilical vein endothelial cells (GEO GSE133751) identified 203 differentially expressed genes dominated by interferon-stimulated genes. A STRING protein–protein interaction network (176 nodes, 3,210 edges) and composite master-regulator centrality score identified 15 hubs, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Open Targets analysis identified six druggable hubs and 12 repurposing candidates in four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 immunopathology. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased CXCL10, an effect that follows from modelling CXCL10 as an IRF1-driven rather than STAT1-driven output. Combining IFN-β with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral efficacy and immunopathology control, although in the present model the antiviral gain of this combination derives entirely from its interferon component. This mechanistically grounded, evidence-ranked framework prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.

papers.title: Andes Hantavirus human-to-human transmission dynamics and preparedness scenarios
papers.abstract: Abstract Human-to-human transmission of the Andes virus (ANDV), which causes the deadly Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome, has been documented in several outbreaks, but remains insufficiently characterized to ensure preparedness against future emergence. Here, we integrate epidemiological data from historical outbreaks and from the 2026 MV Hondius outbreak with a stochastic network-based transmission model to quantify ANDV epidemic potential and control requirements. We estimate a reproduction number of R 0 = 2.30 (95% CI: 1.33–3.27), supporting sustained human transmission. Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis show that variation in transmissibility and incubation period mainly affects outbreak timing and size, while superspreading events can substantially alter the epidemic evolution. Model analysis and simulations further reveal how contact-network structure strongly modulates outbreak size, with close-contact clustering facilitating containment. Due to the virus characteristics, rapid identification and isolation can effectively suppress outbreaks, even more effectively than in the case of COVID-19, whereas pre-symptomatic transmission or increased mixing could substantially increase risk. Our results provide a quantitative framework for ANDV preparedness and highlight the most critical transmission features for future surveillance.

papers.title: Incidence, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and pharmacological management of the 2026 Andes virus outbreak.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus is considered as a fatal zoonotic pathogen that can be commonly transmitted from rodents to humans. However, the Andes virus (ANDV), a type of New World hantavirus, can also be transmitted from human to human. It is the cause of the 2026 hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship. Hantavirus can rapidly progress to a severe respiratory distress, known as hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). Since there is no specific treatment or approved vaccine for hantavirus infection, early diagnosis and critical care support are essential. In cases of HCPS, depending on the severity of the infection, it is important to administer antipyretics, vasopressors, fluid therapy, cardiopulmonary support, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy (RRT) in a timely manner. Currently, there is no approved vaccine in the United States or Europe. However, various vaccine technologies, including inactivated, DNA, mRNA, viral vector and protein-based vaccines, are in the preclinical and clinical phases. Preventive actions, including patient isolation and physical distancing, are crucial to avoiding widespread transmission.

analysis.background: Hantavirus is a fatal zoonotic pathogen transmitted from rodents, and the Andes virus uniquely spreads human‑to‑human, motivating review of the 2026 outbreak.
analysis.main_directions: The review covers transmission dynamics, clinical management of HCPS, vaccine development pipelines, and infection‑control measures.
analysis.current_state: The 2026 Andes virus outbreak on a cruise ship caused severe HCPS; no specific antiviral or approved vaccine exists, so care relies on supportive therapies.
analysis.gaps: There is no licensed vaccine, therapeutic options are limited, and human‑to‑human transmission mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
analysis.future_research: Prioritize pre‑clinical and clinical testing of inactivated, DNA, mRNA, viral‑vector and protein vaccines, and evaluate isolation and distancing strategies to curb spread.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus is a fatal zoonotic pathogen transmitted from rodents, and the Andes virus uniquely spreads human-to-human, motivating review of the 2026 outbreak. Main directions: The review covers transmission dynamics, clinical management of HCPS, vaccine development pipelines, and infection-control measures. Current state: The 2026 Andes virus outbreak on a cruise ship caused severe HCPS; no specific antiviral or approved vaccine exists, so care relies on supportive therapies. Gaps: There is no licensed vaccine, therapeutic options are limited, and human-to-human transmission mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Future research: Prioritize pre-clinical and clinical testing of inactivated, DNA, mRNA, viral-vector and protein vaccines, and evaluate isolation and distancing strategies to curb spread.

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒 是一种致命的动物源性病原体,源自啮齿动物;安第斯病毒 独特地实现人际传播,促使对2026年疫情进行综述。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 综述涵盖传播动力学、汉坦病毒心肺综合征的临床管理、疫苗研发管线以及感染控制措施。
analysis_zh.gaps: 缺口:没有获批疫苗,治疗方案有限,人际传播机制尚未完全理解。
analysis_zh.future_research: 未来研究:优先开展灭活、DNA、mRNA、病毒载体和蛋白疫苗的临床前及临床试验,并评估隔离和社交距离策略以遏制传播。

papers.title: Burning down the mouse: Effects of wildfire and post-fire reseeding on Sin Nombre virus prevalence in its reservoir host
papers.abstract: Abstract Worldwide, physical habitats and biological communities are being reshaped by wildfire. Such changes have obvious potential to alter pathogen ecology, yet few studies, outside of those focused on ectoparasites, have tested the effects of wildfire on pathogen prevalence in wildlife. Even fewer have focused on the impacts of strategies for post-fire remediation on pathogen circulation. analysis_zh.background: 摘要指出,全球野火正在重塑栖息地和生物群落,且很少有研究探讨野火——尤其是火后修复——如何影响野生动物中的病原体流行率。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究在新墨西哥北部使用匹配的烧毁、未烧毁和火后重新播种地点,对411只西部鹿鼠进行RT‐qPCR筛查Sin Nombre病毒,并分析相对鼠类丰度、个体感染概率、地点级流行率及病毒负荷。

papers.title: Epidemiological characteristics and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, China, 2019-2025.
papers.abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease. To characterize the spatiotemporal epidemiological patterns of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula from 2019 to 2025 and to explore the influence of meteorological factors on its spatiotemporal heterogeneity, the present study conducted relevant analyses with the aim of providing evidence for the development of scientific and effective HFRS prevention and control measures. Method Data on HFRS were collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System. Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis and spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression model analysis were employed to examine the incidence of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region from 2019 to 2025. Result From 2019 to 2025, a total of 1,492 cases of HFRS were reported in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The peak incidence period occurs annually from October to January of the following year. The age distribution is concentrated among those aged 45-74, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.58:1, and the occupational distribution is dominated by farmers. Overall, the spatial distribution pattern shows higher rates in the north and west compared to the south and east. Analysis using a join-point regression model indicates that the incidence rate showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021, with an annual percentage change (APC) of 40.70% (95% CI: -15.72 to 134.88%, p = 0.103); however, this upward trend was not statistically significant. The incidence rate showed a downward trend from 2021 to 2025, with an APC of -13.60% (95% CI: -25.55 to 0.26%, p = 0.052); this downward trend was marginally significant. Analysis of global spatial autocorrelation revealed that, with the exception of 2019 (Moran's I = 0.205, p = 0.052) and 2022 (Moran's I = 0.189, p = 0.059), the incidence of HFRS showed spatial clustering in all other years (all with p p Conclusion From 2019 to 2025, HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region exhibited characteristics of seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Health education should be strengthened among key populations, such as middle-aged and older male farmers, and prevention and control measures should be intensified in high-risk areas, including central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao. Future prevention and control strategies should incorporate region-specific climatic characteristics to formulate targeted interventions.

source_records.title: Epidemiological characteristics and spatiotemporal heterogeneity of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, China, 2019-2025.
source_records.abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a serious zoonotic infectious disease. To characterize the spatiotemporal epidemiological patterns of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula from 2019 to 2025 and to explore the influence of meteorological factors on its spatiotemporal heterogeneity, the present study conducted relevant analyses with the aim of providing evidence for the development of scientific and effective HFRS prevention and control measures. Method Data on HFRS were collected through the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Information System. Descriptive epidemiology, Joinpoint regression analysis, spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatiotemporal clustering analysis and spatiotemporal geographically weighted regression model analysis were employed to examine the incidence of HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region from 2019 to 2025. Result From 2019 to 2025, a total of 1,492 cases of HFRS were reported in the Jiaodong Peninsula region, with an average annual incidence rate of 1.073 per 100,000 people. The peak incidence period occurs annually from October to January of the following year. The age distribution is concentrated among those aged 45-74, with a male-to-female ratio of 2.58:1, and the occupational distribution is dominated by farmers. Overall, the spatial distribution pattern shows higher rates in the north and west compared to the south and east. Analysis using a join-point regression model indicates that the incidence rate showed an upward trend from 2019 to 2021, with an annual percentage change (APC) of 40.70% (95% CI: -15.72 to 134.88%, p = 0.103); however, this upward trend was not statistically significant. The incidence rate showed a downward trend from 2021 to 2025, with an APC of -13.60% (95% CI: -25.55 to 0.26%, p = 0.052); this downward trend was marginally significant. Analysis of global spatial autocorrelation revealed that, with the exception of 2019 (Moran's I = 0.205, p = 0.052) and 2022 (Moran's I = 0.189, p = 0.059), the incidence of HFRS showed spatial clustering in all other years (all with p p Conclusion From 2019 to 2025, HFRS in the Jiaodong Peninsula region exhibited characteristics of seasonal prevalence, spatiotemporal clustering, and spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Health education should be strengthened among key populations, such as middle-aged and older male farmers, and prevention and control measures should be intensified in high-risk areas, including central-western Yantai and northern Qingdao. Future prevention and control strategies should incorporate region-specific climatic characteristics to formulate targeted interventions.

analysis.results: From 2019 to 2025, 1,492 HFRS cases were reported (average annual incidence 1.073 per 100,000); peak incidence occurred October‑January; cases were concentrated in persons aged 45‑74, male‑to‑female ratio 2.58:1, mainly farmers; higher rates were observed in the north and west; Joinpoint analysis showed a non‑significant upward trend 2019‑2021 (APC 40.70%, 95% CI ‑15.72 to 134.88, p = 0.103) and a marginally significant downward trend 2021‑2025 (APC ‑13.60%, 95% CI ‑25.55 to 0.26, p = 0.052); spatial autocorrelation indicated clustering in most years.

Methods: Using Chinese CDC data, the authors analyzed 2019‑2025 cases in the Jiaodong Peninsula with descriptive, Joinpoint, spatial autocorrelation, clustering, and geographically weighted regression methods.
